title: Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation
title_zh: 精神科医生是否具备“蛛网感”？临床印象作为人际贝叶斯期望的违背
abstract: Abstract Psychiatric diagnosis depends on the clinician’s ability to infer mental states from complex and dynamically evolving interpersonal signals. During the psychiatric interview, clinicians do not only collect explicit symptoms; they continuously sample a rich array of non-verbal and paralinguistic cues including gaze, prosody, affective reciprocity, and interactional timing. These signals are central to psychiatric assessment, yet their contribution to diagnostic reasoning remains poorly formalized. In this Review, we propose a computational account of clinical impressions in psychiatry. We integrate evidence from phenomenological psychopathology, social cognition, and computational neuroscience. We argue that such impressions may arise when the clinician’s generative model of social interaction is persistently disconfirmed by subtle deviations in interpersonal behaviour, generating high-level social prediction errors experienced as a sense of incongruity or failed attunement. We formalize this process as VIBE: Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation. VIBE denotes a pre-reflective epistemic signal generated when observed interpersonal cues deviate from the clinician’s expected model of social reciprocity. It is not a diagnostic criterion but orients hypothesis generation by drawing attention to disturbances in interpersonal predictability. We hypothesize that VIBE may constitute a transdiagnostic mechanism: different disorders, from schizophrenia to autism spectrum disorder and mood disorders, may disrupt distinct dimensions of interpersonal prediction. The Praecox Feeling, first described by Rümke in 1942, can be read as the earliest clinical formalization of this process and as its schizophrenia-spectrum instance, in which the profile of interpersonal violations is consistent enough to be clinically recognizable. This framework recasts the diagnostic impression as an embodied inferential process rather than an opaque subjective faculty. Teaching clinicians to articulate, examine, and recalibrate these impressions could strengthen diagnostic reasoning, reduce bias, and improve therapeutic attunement. VIBE provides a bridge between phenomenological psychopathology and computational neuroscience, and offers a tractable, empirically testable model for studying the neurocomputational basis of psychiatric clinical judgement.
abstract_zh: 精神病学诊断依赖临床医生从复杂且动态演变的人际信号中推断心理状态。在精神科访谈期间，临床医生不仅收集显性症状，还持续采样丰富的非语言和语调线索，包括凝视、语调、情感互惠和互动节奏。这些信号是精神评估的核心，但其对诊断推理的贡献尚未得到充分形式化。在本综述中，我们提出了精神科临床印象的计算模型。我们整合了现象学精神病理学、社会认知和计算神经科学的证据。我们认为，当临床医生关于社会互动的生成模型被人际行为的细微偏差持续否定时，可能产生此类印象，从而产生高层次的社会预测误差，表现为不协调感或失调的共振。我们将此过程形式化为 VIBE：人际贝叶斯期望的违背（Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation）。VIBE 表示当观察到的人际线索偏离临床医生预期的社会互惠模型时产生的前反思性认知信号。它不是诊断标准，而是通过将注意力聚焦在人际可预测性失调上来引导假设生成。我们假设 VIBE 可能构成一种跨诊断机制：从精神分裂症到自闭症谱系障碍和情绪障碍等不同疾病，可能破坏人际预测的不同维度。Rümke 在 1942 年首次描述的 Praecox Feeling 可以被解读为该过程的最早临床形式化，也是其精神分裂症谱系实例，在该实例中，人际违背的特征足够一致，能够被临床识别。该框架将诊断印象重新定义为一种具身推理过程，而非晦涩的主观能力。教导临床医生阐述、检视并重新校准这些印象，可能加强诊断推理、减少偏见并提升治疗共振。VIBE 为现象学精神病理学与计算神经科学之间搭建桥梁，并提供了一个可操作、可经验检验的模型，用于研究精神临床判断的神经计算基础。
